THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.
The insurer as well as claimant are in appeal.

2. The insurer contends that the finding of the Tribunal that the driver of the car was alone negligent for the accident is incorrect, since the evidence on record indicates that the car hit a parked lorry.
It is also contended that the driver of the car had been acquitted and therefore, certain degree of negligence ought to be attributed to the driver of the parked lorry.
It is also contended that the sums awarded towards injury are incorrect and the sums assessed as the monthly income of the deceased is incorrect.
3. As far as the aspect of negligence is concerned, the police laid a chargesheet against the driver of the car in which both the injured as well as the deceased were travelling.
4. The injured claimant has deposed that the accident occurred solely due to the negligence of the driver of the car.
This is supported by the fact that the police laid a chargesheet against the driver of the car.

The sketch that is produced as Ex.P-7 also indicates that the lorry was parked on the shoulder of the road and despite that the driver of the car had collided with this lorry which had been parked on the shoulder of the road.
5. In my view, in the light of the evidence on record, the finding of the Tribunal that the driver of the car was alone responsible for the accident cannot be found fault with.

It is also to be stated here that it is the choice of the claimant to proceed against the tortfeasor that they think was responsible for the accident and it would be permissible for the not insurer to contend that both the tortfeasors should be arrayed.
In that view of the matter, the ground of negligence urged would be unavailable to the insurer.

6. As far as compensation awarded for the death of Dayanand, a 23 year old, the Tribunal on taking note of the salary certificate and evidence of the employer has assessed the income at Rs.12,061/-
per month.

It is to be stated here that the claimant was working in a Private Limited Company and the representative of the Company who deposed as P.W.2 has stated that the salary was being paid to the Bank account of the deceased.
7.
In that view of the matter, the assessment of monthly income cannot be found fault with.
The Tribunal has also properly added the future prospects and has applied the correct multiplier and awarded Rs.20,23,936/-.
In my view, there is no justification to interfere with the quantum of compensation also.
Bhuvaneshwara.

K vs Rajanikanth on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160398673/
5 8.

As far as the claim regarding the injured claimant is concerned, an appeal is preferred by the claimant contending that the assessment of disability at 15% would be incorrect, since the evidence indicates that the claimant had suffered not only head injury, but he had lost the hearing capability in his left ear.
9. It is also stated that the sums awarded are on the lower side.
He also stated that the income determined by the Tribunal was improper and the sums awarded under the other heads are also on the lower side.
10. The Doctor, who was examined as C.W.2 has stated that the claimant has suffered the hearing disability to the extent of 67.5% to the left ear as per pure tone audiometer.
11. In other words, it is the evidence of the Doctor that the claimant has virtually lost the ability to hear from his left ear.
The evidence of the other Doctor C.W.1 also states that the claimant has suffered cognitive disability.

12. In my view, having regard to the avocation of the claimant as a Fitter and taking into consideration the injuries suffered by claimant, it would be appropriate to determine the whole body disability at 30%.
13. The Tribunal has determined the monthly income, notionally at Rs.8,000/-.

Since there is no credible documentary evidence to ascertain the actual monthly income, it would be appropriate and prudent to adopt the monthly income determined by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority,
which, for the accident of the year 2016, would be Rs.9,500/-.
14.

Since the claimant was aged 25 years and the disability suffered is at 30%, 40% is to be added towards future prospects to determine monthly income of the claimant for awarding compensation towards 'loss of future income' which comes to Rs.13,300/-.
15.
As the claimant was aged 25 years, a multiplier of '18' would have to be applied.

Consequently,
the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.8,61,840/- (Rs.13,300/- x 12 x '18' x 30%) towards 'loss of future income' .
As a consequence, the amount of Rs.24,000/- awarded by the Tribunal towards 'loss of income during the laid up period' would also stand enhanced to Rs.28,500/- (Rs.9,500/- X 3 months).
17. Having regard to the injuries suffered by the claimant, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.75,000/- towards 'pain and suffering' as against Rs.50,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

18. Having regard to the lasting effects of the injuries on the claimant, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs. 1,00,000/- towards 'loss of amenities', as against the sum of Rs.35,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
Bhuvaneshwara.

K vs Rajanikanth on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160398673/
6 19.

Having regard to the length of the stay of the claimant in the hospital, the sums awarded under the heads 'Transportation charges', 'food and nourishment' and 'attendant charges' are just and proper and stands affirmed.

The sums awarded as medical expenses by the Tribunal, being based on documentary evidence,
does not call for modification and hence confirmed.
21. The evidence on record also indicates that the claimant was a bachelor.

Obviously the loss of hearing ability in one ear would have effect on marriage prospects and therefore, Rs.75,000/- is awarded towards 'loss of marriage prospects'.
22.

Consequently, the award of the Tribunal is modified and the following sums are awarded as compensation:
 Sl. Particulars Award by Award by  No. Tribunal this Court  (Rs.) (Rs.)

1 . Pain and sufferings 50,000/- 75,000/-
 2. Medical expenses 1,63,396/- 1,63,396/-
 3. Food and nourishment 20,000/- 20,000/-
4 . Transportation
charges

5. Loss of amenities in 35,000/- 1,00,000/-
 life  6. Attendant charges 9,000/- 9,000/-
 7. Loss of future income 2,59,200/- 8,61,840/-
 8. Loss of income during 24,000/- 28,500/-
 laid up period  - 12 -  9. Loss of marriage - 75,000/-
 prospects  Total 5,80,596/- 13,52,736/-
Bhuvaneshwara.

7 23.

Thus, the claimant is held entitled to the total compensation of Rs.13,52,736/- as against Rs.5,80,596/-, along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
24. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
25. The apportionment of the compensation amount would be in terms of the award of the Tribunal.

The amount in deposit, if any, shall be transferred to the Tribunal forthwith.
27. The appeals filed by insurer are dismissed and the appeal filed by claimant is accordingly allowed in part.

Sd/-
JUDGE HNM Bhuvaneshwara.

Since the claimant was aged 25 years and the disability suffered is at 30%, 40% is to be added towards future prospects to determine monthly income of the claimant for awarding compensation towards 'loss of future income' which comes to Rs.13,300/-.
15.

Consequently,
the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.8,61,840/- (Rs.13,300/- x 12 x '18' x 30%) towards 'loss of future income' .
As a consequence, the amount of Rs.24,000/- awarded by the Tribunal towards 'loss of income during the laid up period' would also stand enhanced to Rs.28,500/- (Rs.9,500/- X 3 months).
17. Having regard to the injuries suffered by the claimant, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.75,000/- towards 'pain and suffering' as against Rs.50,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

18. Having regard to the lasting effects of the injuries on the claimant, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs. 1,00,000/- towards 'loss of amenities', as against the sum of Rs.35,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.

Having regard to the length of the stay of the claimant in the hospital, the sums awarded under the heads 'Transportation charges', 'food and nourishment' and 'attendant charges' are just and proper and stands affirmed.

The sums awarded as medical expenses by the Tribunal, being based on documentary evidence,
does not call for modification and hence confirmed.

Obviously the loss of hearing ability in one ear would have effect on marriage prospects and therefore, Rs.75,000/- is awarded towards 'loss of marriage prospects'.
22.
